newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices hold, helped by gas, weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices hold, helped by gas, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held fairly steady again Thursday in slack activity, helped by forecasts for better cooling demand and firmer city gate gas prices that left resid more competitive, sources said.

"We're keeping a close eye on gas, and with some heat coming in and crude holding, I don't expect fuel prices to come off anymore right now," said one East Coast utility source, adding it would take some extended heat to drive utilities back into the market.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $15.75-16.00 a barrel, with July paper still around $15.50-60.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour inched into the low-$17s amid prospects for better cooling demand.
High sulphurs in New York held steady, with 2.2 percent still quoted at $14.30-55, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices also were little changed, with one percent still at $16.00, while three percent eased slightly to $14.25.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate gas prices again firmed by a couple of cents Thursday to the $2.47/mmBtu area, or $15.56 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed slightly to about $2.23/mmBtu, or $14.05 a barrel.
